events.headline: Houthi rebels kill at least 100 in offensive toward Bab al-Mandab strait, Yemen
events.summary: Fighting between Iran-backed Houthi rebels and Yemeni government forces has intensified since Thursday, with at least 100 people killed as Houthis push toward a key strait.

events.headline: US diesel prices hit all-time high amid Iran conflict
events.summary: US diesel prices have reached a record high, driven by the surge in wholesale oil prices since the Iran conflict began at the end of February.

events.headline: Two Palestinian teenagers shot dead in West Bank village amid settler-military raid
events.summary: Palestinian teenagers Omar al-Naasan and Khalil Abu Alia were shot dead when Israeli settlers and soldiers entered a village in the occupied West Bank. The father of one of the teens told the BBC he expects his sons to be killed.

events.headline: US August jobs report seen as signal for Fed inflation policy, BlackRock says
events.summary: BlackRock portfolio manager Jeffrey Rosenberg said the August US employment report is significant primarily for its implications on inflation and Federal Reserve monetary policy.

events.headline: Gold falls as strong US payrolls fuel Fed rate hike bets
events.summary: Gold prices fell after a stronger-than-anticipated increase in US payrolls drove bets that the Federal Reserve will be forced to raise interest rates this year.

events.headline: Oil surges on renewed US-Iran fighting, Strait of Hormuz disruption fears
events.summary: Oil prices were on track for a weekly surge as renewed fighting between the US and Iran heightened concerns about prolonged disruptions to energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz.

events.headline: US launches fresh strikes on Iranian military targets amid 'forever war' concerns
events.summary: The United States has launched fresh attacks on military targets in Iran, aiming to prevent Tehran from rebuilding destroyed military capabilities. Analysts warn the campaign risks becoming a sustained cycle of reconstruction followed by renewed attacks.

events.headline: Norway seizes Russian ship Professor Molchanov over Naftogaz court order
events.summary: Norwegian authorities seized the Russian vessel Professor Molchanov near Svalbard following a court order sought by Ukraine's Naftogaz to compensate for damages Russia refused to pay. Russia has protested the seizure.

events.headline: Israel seizes strategic Ali al-Taher ridge from Hezbollah in south Lebanon
events.summary: Israel's Defence Minister Israel Katz announced that Israeli forces have seized the Ali al-Taher ridge in southern Lebanon from Hezbollah, a highland about 10 kilometres from the Israeli border. The area had been targeted by Israeli strikes in recent weeks despite an existing ceasefire, and Hezbollah has not confirmed losing the position.

events.headline: UK reasserts Falklands sovereignty after Milei and Trump remarks
events.summary: Britain reaffirmed the Falkland Islands 'are British' after Argentine President Javier Milei suggested shifting US neutrality could favor Argentina's claim, following comments by President Trump. The dispute over the islands' sovereignty resurfaced in headlines.

events.headline: Oil prices surge as US-Iran hostilities resume, Strait of Hormuz remains blocked
events.summary: Renewed US-Iran hostilities have reignited fears of oil supply disruption, with prices on track for their steepest weekly gain since mid-July, up 7.6%, as the conflict enters its seventh month. The Strait of Hormuz, through which 25% of world oil supply passes, has been blocked since the start of the conflict.

events.headline: Houthis advance toward Bab al-Mandab Strait port city amid escalating ground fighting
events.summary: Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi militia appear to be pushing to seize control of a port city near the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a key global trade chokepoint, as ground fighting escalates in the region.

events.headline: Ukraine's Budanov advocates negotiated settlement as Russia-Ukraine talks set to resume
events.summary: Kyrylo Budanov, a former Ukrainian military intelligence chief, has advocated for a negotiated settlement with Russia. Talks between the two sides are expected to resume this month.

events.headline: Dutch central bank repatriates 90 tons of gold from New York Fed citing geopolitical unrest
events.summary: The Netherlands' central bank moved approximately 90 tons of gold out of the Federal Reserve Bank in New York, citing 'geopolitical unrest'. It is the second European nation this year to announce a decrease or elimination of its U.S. gold holdings.

events.headline: Chinese researchers claim uranium extraction from seawater at 8 times US target rate
events.summary: A team from the Chinese Academy of Sciences in Qingdao developed a material called PhosCage that extracts uranium from seawater at a rate several times higher than the target set by the US Department of Energy. The advance could position China at the forefront of efforts to tap seawater as a nuclear fuel source.

events.headline: Fuel and petrochemical prices outpace crude oil, disrupting global supply chains like potato chip packaging
events.summary: Fuel and petrochemical prices are rising faster than crude oil, with downstream effects reaching consumer goods such as Japanese snack brand Calbee, which changed its packaging due to supply chain pressures. The report examines the causes and durability of this price divergence.

events.headline: Burkina Faso tests Chinese Sky Dragon 30 surface-to-air missile system
events.summary: Burkina Faso tested what observers identify as a Chinese-made Sky Dragon 30 surface-to-air missile system, with footage released by the Burkinabe president's office showing multiple missiles fired from a mobile launcher. This signals expanding Chinese military equipment exports into the Sahel region.

events.headline: China and US military commanders resume Taiwan Strait command-level talks in Canada after 2-year break
events.summary: Chinese General Yang Zhibin, commander of the PLA Eastern Theatre Command, met US Admiral Samuel Paparo at the Indo-Pacific Chiefs of Defence Conference in Canada, ending a two-year break in command-level military contact between China and the US regarding the Taiwan Strait.

events.headline: Body of convicted war criminal Ratko Mladic returned to Serbia with military honours
events.summary: The body of Bosnian Serb war criminal Ratko Mladic arrived in Serbia from The Hague and was received with military honours, carried by six soldiers with the casket draped in the Serbian flag. Mladic's son Darko and Serbia's Justice Minister Nenad Vujic accompanied the transfer.

events.headline: Putin hardens resolve for military win in Ukraine after CIA Director Ratcliffe's Moscow visit fails
events.summary: CIA Director John Ratcliffe's visit to Moscow failed to persuade Russian President Vladimir Putin to stop the war in Ukraine, and may have instead hardened his resolve to pursue a military victory. Following the visit, Putin escalated strikes on Ukraine.

events.headline: Unconfirmed PLA Naval Exercise Reports Near Taiwan Surface on Chinese Forums
